verdict.rationale: FireHydrant clearly keeps a per-incident timeline: AI-drafted retrospectives analyze "the incident's timeline" and produce timelines (docs-80, docs-35). The AI Scribe captures discussions and decisions from incident bridges and Zoom chat (docs-64, docs-29, docs-79), and responders can post notes and updates via `/fh update` or Command Center (docs-65). However, no doc explicitly says alerts, runbook actions and Slack chat decisions are auto-logged to the timeline, and editing or annotating the timeline afterwards is only implied via retrospective editing (docs-78). Missing for 10: explicit documentation of automatic capture of alerts, actions and Slack messages into the timeline; documented post-incident timeline editing or annotation; independent or hands-on corroboration.
